claims.claim_ar: حصر الذكر في حال التضرع والخفية، أي تقييد الذكر بصيغة الخشوع الداخلي وعدم الجهر
claims.claim_en: Restriction (hasr/qasr): the remembrance is constrained to supplication and secrecy — i.e., it confines remembrance to inward reverence and not to loud public utterance.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Directs the worshipper to an inward, humble mode of remembrance and implicitly critiques ostentatious/loud devotion.

claims.claim_ar: تباين/تضاد بين الخفيّ والجهر؛ الآية تضع مقابل الخفية (الخشوع الداخلي) ما يعارضها من الجهر، مما يؤكد التباين الأخلاقي والوظيفي بينهما
claims.claim_en: Antithetical pairing (tibaq): the verse contrasts secrecy (inner humility) with loudness; by juxtaposing inner reverence and loud vocalization it highlights the moral and functional opposition between them.
claims.needs_review_reason: Classification as 'tibaq' (pairing of opposites) is plausible here but could also be labeled as muqabalah or another contrast-term in other commentators; needs cross-check with Jurjani/Sakkaki/Baqillani treatments.
claims.rhetorical_effect: By opposing hiddenness and loudness the wording pressures the reader/listener to prefer modest, inward devotion and to reject showy displays; it also strengthens admonitory tone.

warnings: Source material provided is limited mainly to the Zamakhshari chunk that treats تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً and critiques loud praying (الصراخ والصياح في الدعاء). Claims are based on that chunk; other classical rhetoricians named in the task (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha) were not present among the source_chunks, so mappings/classifications (e.g., tibaq vs muqabalah) should be cross-checked against those authors.
Some device assignments (especially between closely related contrast devices: tibaq vs muqabalah) are interpretive. See needs_review_reason on the relevant claim for details.
